audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL state transitions (block validation, EVM stack, difficulty, hash storage, withdrawal requests, cryptographic operations), CL interactions (proof engine, release lifecycle), and cross-layer interfaces (Engine API, execution payloads). Both EL and CL are in scope.

out_of_scope: Execution Layer internals beyond Engine API interface

threats: Malicious calldata to precompiles or system contracts
Requesting historical data to exhaust resources

cl_vectors.entry_point: External APIs (MEV-Boost relay, proof engines, checkpoint providers)

misclassified_entities.reason: SYSTEM_ADDRESS (0xff..fe) is an internal reserved address used by block processing, not a true external entity. It is part of the EL's internal system call mechanism.
Spec maintainer is part of the specification governance process, not a runtime external entity interacting with EL/CL software. Relevant for supply-chain analysis but not for runtime trust modeling.
Generic attacker entity is a threat model concept, not a specific external entity with a defined entry point. Attack vectors are captured in archetypal_attack_vectors instead.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P (devp2p)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: devp2p protocol (block propagation, transaction relay, historical data requests)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer nodes communicate over unauthenticated P2P network. Any peer can send malformed blocks, invalid transactions, or malicious historical data requests. Covers EXT-PEER-NODE, EXT-REQUESTING-PEER from EIP-4444 and Constantinople subgraphs.

trusted_external_entities.name: User/DApp via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users and DApps submit transactions and queries via public RPC. No authentication required. Covers EXT-TX-SUBMITTER, EXT-DAPP, EXT-CALLING-CONTRACT, EXT-NORMAL-CALLER, EXT-SIGNATURE-PROVIDER (via transaction signatures), EXT-PRECOMPILE-CALLER.

trusted_external_entities.name: Withdrawal Credential Owner via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Withdrawal credential holders submit requests via standard transactions. Authorization is verified on CL side by checking source_address against withdrawal credentials, but EL must treat all callers as untrusted. Covers EXT-WITHDRAWAL-CREDENTIAL-OWNER, EXT-CALLER.

trusted_external_entities.name: Node Operator via Configuration
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Client configuration (weak subjectivity checkpoint, CLI flags)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Node operators provide initial configuration including weak subjectivity checkpoints. They have local access to the node, which provides some trust basis, but checkpoint data must still be validated against known chain state. A compromised checkpoint enables long-range attacks.

trusted_external_entities.name: External Historical Data Provider via Out-of-Band
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Out-of-band data retrieval (IPFS, Portal Network, The Graph, torrent)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External data providers supply historical blockchain data after EIP-4444 pruning. Data is retrieved over unauthenticated channels and must be validated against known state roots. Covers EXT-DATA-PROVIDER.

trusted_external_entities.name: External Proof Engine via Beacon API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Proof engines deliver execution proofs asynchronously via the Beacon API. The API endpoint should be access-controlled, providing an authentication basis, but proof content must be cryptographically verified. A compromised proof engine could submit forged proofs. Covers EXT-PROOF-ENGINE, EXT-BEACON-API-CLIENT, EXT-PROVER.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer (Miner) via P2P
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P network (block propagation with difficulty header)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Miners produce blocks with difficulty values that must be independently validated. A malicious miner could submit blocks with incorrect difficulty. Pre-merge only (EIP-5133). Covered by EXT-MINER.

trusted_external_entities.name: Serialized Data Source via P2P/Network
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P network or API (SSZ-encoded container bytes)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: SSZ-encoded progressive containers (EIP-7495) received from network sources must be fully validated including schema validation, field count checks, and Merkle proof verification. Covers EXT-DATA-SOURCE.

trusted_external_entities.name: Light Client / Smart Contract Verifier
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Merkle proof submission (EIP-7495 progressive container proofs)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Light clients submit Merkle proofs for verification. They are consumers of the proof system, but the proofs they present may come from untrusted sources and require full verification. Covers EXT-LIGHT-CLIENT.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full block header and body validation required: block number, timestamp, gas limit, gas used, extra data, parent hash, difficulty (pre-merge), PoW (pre-merge). All data from peers is potentially malicious.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: devp2p historical data requests (GetBlockHeaders, GetBlockBodies, GetReceipts)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Requests must be bounded by HISTORY_PRUNE_EPOCHS window. Resource exhaustion prevention required for serving peers.

Full transaction validation required: intrinsic gas, sender recovery, nonce check, balance check. All calldata is potentially malicious including calls to precompiles (P-256, ECDSA) and system contracts (EIP-2935 history, EIP-7002 withdrawals).

EL validates: input format (exactly 56 bytes), fee payment (msg.value >= current_fee). CL validates: source_address matches validator's withdrawal credentials. Dynamic fee mechanism must resist spam attacks.
Checkpoint must be validated against known chain state. Must be within weak subjectivity period. Invalid checkpoint enables long-range attacks and syncing to invalid chain.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Out-of-band historical data retrieval (IPFS, Portal Network, indexers)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: All historical data must be verified against known state roots or accumulator proofs. Data integrity cannot be assumed from the transport channel.

API access must be restricted to authorized proof engines. Proof content must be cryptographically verified via verify_execution_proof(). Proof type must match requested ProofAttributes. Timeout handling required for missing/delayed proofs.
Block difficulty must be independently recalculated using correct formula (including EIP-5133 bomb delay offset). Stated difficulty must match computed expected difficulty exactly.

Full schema validation required: non-empty container, max 256 fields, no trailing zeros in active_fields, field count matches active bits. Deserialized containers must have absent fields defaulted to zero. Merkle root must include active_fields mix-in.

Full proof path verification required. active_fields mix-in must be verified to prevent collision between absent fields and zero values. Gindex stability ensures backward compatibility but proofs from untrusted sources must be fully validated.
